title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Word2Vec: CBOW and Skip-gram)
outputs: Dense vector representations (embeddings) for each word in the vocabulary
pseudocode:
1. Preprocess corpus: tokenize, build vocabulary (words appearing ≥ min_count)
2. Initialize word embedding matrix W (vocab_size × embedding_dim) randomly
3. For each epoch:
    4. For each word w_t in corpus:
        5. Extract context window: w_{t-C}...w_{t-1}, w_{t+1}...w_{t+C}
        6. CBOW variant:
            7. Compute context vector: mean of embeddings of context words
            8. Predict center word w_t using softmax (or hierarchical softmax)
            9. Update embeddings via backprop to maximize log P(w_t | context)
        10. Skip-gram variant:
            11. For each context word w_c in window:
                12. Use embedding of w_t to predict w_c
                13. Update embeddings via backprop to maximize log P(w_c | w_t)
        14. Use negative sampling: sample k negative words, update to distinguish true context from noise
    15. Decay learning rate linearly
16. Return trained embedding matrix W
key_equations: CBOW objective: maximize log P(w_t | w_{t-C}, ..., w_{t+C}) = log softmax(W · mean(context_embeddings))
Skip-gram objective: maximize Σ_{c in context} log P(w_c | w_t) = Σ log softmax(W · embedding(w_t))
Negative sampling: log σ(v'_{w_O}^T v_{w_I}) + Σ_{i=1}^k E_{w_i ~ P_n(w)} [log σ(-v'_{w_i}^T v_{w_I})]
Hierarchical softmax: replaces full softmax with binary tree, reducing complexity from O(V) to O(log V)
evaluation_dataset: Google News corpus (6B tokens), restricted vocabulary test sets for semantic-syntactic word relationships (e.g., 'king - man + woman ≈ queen'), Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge
toy_dataset_suggestion: text8 dataset (first 100MB of cleaned Wikipedia text, ~17M tokens) or a small subset (e.g., first 1M tokens). Alternatively, use a simple synthetic corpus or the 'Brown' corpus from NLTK (~1M tokens).
key_figure_description: A table or bar chart showing accuracy (%) on the semantic-syntactic word relationship test set (analogies like 'Paris:France :: Rome:Italy') for different architectures (RNNLM, NNLM, CBOW, Skip-gram) and varying embedding dimensions (50, 100, 300). X-axis: model architecture or embedding dimension; Y-axis: accuracy (0-100%). CBOW and Skip-gram should show higher syntactic/semantic accuracy than baseline NNLMs.
notes: For a toy implementation: (1) Use a small corpus (<10M tokens) and vocabulary (<10k words). (2) Implement either CBOW or Skip-gram, not both. (3) Use negative sampling (simpler than hierarchical softmax). (4) Skip DistBelief parallelization. (5) Train for 1 epoch only. (6) Evaluate on a small analogy test set (~100 questions) or nearest-neighbor retrieval. (7) Focus on demonstrating that learned embeddings capture semantic similarity (e.g., 'king' close to 'queen', 'Paris' close to 'France').
